newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CHELSEA HOPING TO BUILD ON CUP SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CHELSEA HOPING TO BUILD ON CUP SUCCESS.

text.p: Saturday's English F.A. Cup Final between Chelsea and Midlesbrough was far from being a classic, but Chelsea ecstatic fans won't mind about that.
Far more important for them is that their team's 2-0 victory over a demoralised Middlesbrough team could launch Chelsea towards a new era of success, and lay the ghosts of Chelsea's past.

Apart from a solitary league title in 1955, and victory in the League Cup a decade later, Chelsea's only other honours came in the early seventies when the team of Peter Osgood, Alan Hudson, Charlie Cooke and David Webb, won the F.A. Cup in 1970 and the European Cup Winners Cup in 1971.
The achievments of that side, whose players have become like deities among the Chelsea faithfull, have hung like a weight around the club's neck.
Steve Clarke, Chelsea's longest-serving player, summed up the feelings of everyone connected with Chelsea after Saturday's well-deserved success.

"I have been here 10 years so I know better than anyone what this success means. Ever since I have been at Chelsea we've constantly had the era of Osgood, Hudson, Cooke and Bonbetti rammed down our throats.

"No-one would belittle their achievements. They helped give the club a special image but their success has been a burden on each Chelsea team since then and it has got worse with each passing year without us winning a trophy. "Now, at last people might stop talking about the team of the 1970s and start talking about the Chelsea of the nineties. That is why it was so vital for us to win the game."

One Chelsea player who helped launch a successful era at another club in similar circumstances was Mark Hughes, who won his fourth Cup winner's medal on Saturday after winning the Cup with Manchester United in 1985, 1990 and 1994.
Hughes was also part of the Manchester United team that won the League title in 1993 -- something United had not done since the days of Law, Best and Charlton 26 years earlier.
He now believes Chelsea can go on to greater successes.

"I see a comparison with Chelsea," he said, "For so long the club has been reflecting on past triumphs. Now we have won something we can really progress, win more things and really fulfill the potential of this club which has under-achieved for far too long."
Middlesbrough have also under-achieved for even longer than Chelsea and by failing to win on Saturday their 121-year wait for their first major trophy continues.
While Chelsea dream of European soccer next season, relegated Middlesbrough will be taking less than glamorous journeys to Port Vale, Reading and Oxford United in the first division.
The match was as good as over after almost 43 seconds when Roberto di Matteo scored to give Chelsea the lead in the quickest Cup Final goal for 102 years and the fastest at Wembley.

Eddie Newton wrapped the victory up with a second seven minutes from time to send Middlesbrough to defeat in their second major final of the season. They lost in the League Cup Final to Leicester a month ago.
Manager Bryan Robson has some tough-talking to do in the next few days with several of Middlesbrough's expensive overseas signings expected to leave.
While Robson's attempt to blend overseas and British talents together ended in failure, Ruud Gullit the Chelsea manager, has made a far better job of the task.
He became the first overseas coach to lead a side to victory in the F.A. Cup Final on Saturday. Could he yet become the first to do so in the League ?
